relations.evidence_quote: The authorised CBAM declarant shall ensure that the total embedded emissions declared in the CBAM declaration submitted pursuant to Article 6 are verified by a verifier accredited pursuant to Article 18, based on the verification principles set out in Annex VI.
action: reviewing and determining the correctness of the CBAM declaration's declared embedded emissions
object: embedded greenhouse gas emissions declared in the CBAM declaration
mediating_function: independently verifying the declarant's declared embedded emissions against the Annex VI verification principles

distinction.note: Accredited verifiers are independent third parties, distinct from the declarant, the Commission and competent authorities.

function.note: Article 8(1) assigns the verification function; Annex VI sets the verification principles they must apply.

regulatory_integration.note: Article 6(2)(d) makes the verification report a mandatory component of the CBAM declaration itself, and Article 7(5) ties the declarant's record-keeping to enabling verifier and Commission/competent-authority review -- the verification function is woven into the same compliance mechanism directed at the declarant.

evidence.note: Anchored across Articles 6, 7, 8, 10, 18 operative text, not recitals.

counterfactual.note: Article 6(2)(d) requires verification reports as mandatory declaration content; removing independent verification would remove the declaration's only assurance mechanism, a legally required element.

relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: routine] The clearest verification-type intermediary in this Act. See REL_C02_002 for the upstream accreditation layer that qualifies verifiers, and uncertainty U9 for the related declarant/operator voluntary-disclosure detail.

relations.evidence_quote: A national accreditation body may, on request, accredit a person to be a verifier for the purpose of this Regulation where it considers, on the basis of the documentation submitted to it, that such person has the capacity to apply the verification principles referred to in Annex VI when performing the tasks of verification of the embedded emissions pursuant to Articles 8 and 10.

R.label: European Commission
R.role: regulator (sets and oversees accreditation conditions by delegated act)

action: specifying and overseeing the conditions for granting, controlling and withdrawing accreditation of verifiers
object: verifiers' qualification to perform embedded-emissions verification
mediating_function: accrediting persons as qualified verifiers, and exercising control, oversight and withdrawal of that accreditation

distinction.note: National accreditation bodies are appointed by each Member State under Regulation (EC) No 765/2008, Article 4(1), and are distinct from the Commission.

function.note: Article 18(2) explicitly assigns the accrediting function; Article 18(3) empowers the Commission to further specify conditions for granting, controlling, and withdrawing that accreditation.

regulatory_integration.note: Accreditation is the legally necessary upstream gate qualifying the verifiers who perform the Article 8 verification function integrated into the declarant's compliance mechanism (REL_C02_001); Article 18(3) confirms this is an ongoing, legally structured oversight relationship, not a one-off registration.

counterfactual.note: Without national accreditation bodies there is no mechanism to qualify or de-qualify verifiers; the verification layer required by Article 6(2)(d) would lack its competence gate.

relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: source_limit] T here is 'verifiers' rather than the declarant -- the same actor type occupies I in REL_C02_001 and T in this relation, illustrating the RIT framework's relational roles. The detailed accreditation regime lives in Regulation (EC) No 765/2008, not reproduced in this corpus; the CBAM-specific competence-scope decision made by the accreditation body under Article 18(2) is, however, itself operative text. Article 18(3)'s 'mutual recognition and peer evaluation of the accreditation bodies' is a related horizontal quality-assurance mechanism among accreditation bodies themselves (see uncertainty U8).

relations.evidence_quote: The customs authorities shall periodically and automatically, in particular by means of the surveillance mechanism established pursuant to Article 56(5) of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, communicate to the Commission specific information on the goods declared for importation.
action: reviewing CBAM declarations and conducting risk-based controls on compliance
object: compliance of imports with the authorised-declarant and declaration requirements
mediating_function: communicating import data that feeds the Commission's risk analysis and review of CBAM declarations

distinction.note: Article 3(14) defines 'customs authorities' separately from 'competent authority' (Article 3(13)); customs administrations are legally distinct bodies within the CBAM architecture.

function.note: Article 25(1)-(4) assigns customs authorities specific gatekeeping and data-transmission duties.

regulatory_integration.note: The transmitted data explicitly feeds the Commission's Article 15 risk-based controls and Article 19 review of CBAM declarations, both directed at declarant compliance.

evidence.note: Anchored in Article 25 and Article 33 operative text.

counterfactual.note: Article 25(1)'s gatekeeping is the only mechanism preventing non-authorised importation; removing the Article 25(2) data feed would blind the Commission's risk-analysis and review process to actual import flows.

relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: routine] Parallel provisions apply during the transitional period (Article 33).

relations.evidence_quote: Goods shall be imported into the customs territory of the Union only by an authorised CBAM declarant.
action: authorising, registering, reviewing declarations, and managing certificate purchase/surrender/repurchase/cancellation
object: compliance with authorisation, declaration and certificate-surrender obligations
relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: routine] Core compliance architecture bundling declaration, registry and certificate-lifecycle obligations. The Commission and Member State competent authorities are treated as joint/parallel regulators rather than one intermediating the other (see uncertainty U3 regarding Article 12).

relations.evidence_quote: An authorised CBAM declarant who fails to surrender, by 31 May of each year, the number of CBAM certificates that corresponds to the emissions embedded in goods imported during the preceding calendar year shall be held liable for the payment of a penalty.
action: imposing and securing payment of penalties for non-compliance
object: failure to surrender CBAM certificates or unauthorised importation
relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: routine] The Commission's preliminary calculation (Article 26(4), cross-referencing Article 19) is the same joint-regulator preliminary-input pattern already captured in REL_C02_004, not a separate intermediary.

relations.evidence_quote: The Commission shall, upon request by an operator of an installation located in a third country, register the information on that operator and on its installation in the CBAM registry referred to in Article 14.

T.label: operators of installations in third countries

action: registering operators and installations and requiring them to determine and verify embedded emissions
object: embedded emissions of goods produced at third-country installations
relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: routine] Operators are a distinct regulated actor from declarants; their voluntary disclosure of verified information to declarants (Article 10(7)) is a procedural detail between two independently regulated targets, not a third-party intermediary structure (see uncertainty U9).

relations.evidence_quote: If a third country or territory has an electricity market which is integrated with the Union internal market for electricity through market coupling, and there is no technical solution for the application of the CBAM to the importation of electricity into the customs territory of the Union from that third country or territory, such importation of electricity from that country or territory shall be exempt from the application of the CBAM, provided that the Commission has assessed that all of the following conditions have been fulfilled in accordance with paragraph 8:

T.label: third countries or territories seeking electricity-market exemption

action: assessing third countries' roadmaps and reports and granting or withdrawing electricity-market exemption from the CBAM
object: third countries' progress on electricity-market and climate-policy alignment conditions
relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: conceptual_boundary] A third country/territory is treated here as a T-like jurisdictional actor based on self-reporting (roadmap, biennial reports) directly to the Commission; no third-party intermediary is involved.

relations.evidence_quote: A Member State or any party that has been affected by, or has benefited from, any of the situations referred to in paragraph 2 may notify the Commission if it is confronted with practices of circumvention. Interested parties other than directly affected or benefited parties, such as environmental organisations and non-governmental organisations, which find concrete evidence of practices of circumvention may also notify the Commission.

I.label: Member States, affected/benefited parties, and interested parties such as environmental organisations and NGOs

T.label: producers, exporters, importers or traders engaged in practices of circumvention

action: monitoring and investigating practices of circumvention
object: practices of circumvention of the CBAM obligations
mediating_function: submitting formally-structured notifications that trigger a mandatory Commission investigation

distinction.note: Notifying parties are distinct from the Commission and from the producers/traders under investigation.

function.note: Article 27(4)-(5) grants a formally defined notification channel with specific content requirements (reasons, data, statistics).

regulatory_integration.note: A compliant notification legally triggers ('the Commission shall initiate an investigation') the Commission's anti-circumvention process.

counterfactual.note: Article 27(3) gives the Commission its own independent 'continuous monitoring... by way of market surveillance or on the basis of any relevant source of information', so the notification channel is one of several detection routes rather than the sole mechanism; the notifier does not itself verify, process or certify anything, unlike the verification/accreditation intermediaries above.

relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: conceptual_boundary] More institutionalised than ordinary lobbying or an NGO publication (formal content requirements, mandatory triggered response), but functionally closer to a complaint/tip channel than to a mediating function like verification or accreditation, since the Commission independently investigates using its own data. Contrast the more strongly institutionalised substantiated-concerns mechanism found in Case 03 (EUDR, Article 31), coded intermediated there for reasons detailed in that case's uncertainty log (U9).

uncertainties.evidence_quote: The Commission shall be assisted by the CBAM Committee. That committee shall be a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.
uncertainties.reasoning: Comitology committee under Regulation (EU) No 182/2011, composed of Member State representatives, exercising a control function over the Commission's implementing power rather than a function directed at declarants; its composition and voting procedures are not reproduced in this corpus.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State in accordance with the principles laid down in the Inter-institutional Agreement of 13 April 2016 on Better Law-Making.
uncertainties.reasoning: Consultation supports the Commission's own rule-making (delegated acts), not target-directed intermediation; parallels the Advisory Board's Article 4 target-setting role excluded in Case 01.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: In addition to the other tasks that it exercises under this Regulation, the Commission shall assist the competent authorities in carrying out their functions and duties under this Regulation and shall coordinate their activities by supporting the exchange of, and issuing guidelines on, best practices within the scope of this Regulation, and by promoting an adequate exchange of information and cooperation between competent authorities as well as between competent authorities and the Commission.
candidate_actors: European Commission (as coordinator of competent authorities)
uncertainties.reasoning: Considered as a candidate regulator-facing intermediary (Commission mediating between 'competent authority as R' and declarant as T), but rejected in favour of treating the Commission and competent authorities as joint/parallel regulators, given the Commission's extensive independent direct regulatory functions elsewhere in the same architecture (registry management, declaration review, implementing acts). Treating the Commission as I here would be inconsistent with its role as R throughout the rest of the Act.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: a forum of countries with carbon pricing instruments or other comparable instruments (‘Climate Club’) should be set up, in order to promote the implementation of ambitious climate policies in all countries and pave the way for a global carbon pricing framework
uncertainties.reasoning: No operative provision in Articles 1-36 establishes or operationalises the Climate Club; it remains a recital-only policy aspiration.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: The Commission, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, shall collect the information necessary with a view to extending the scope of this Regulation as indicated in and pursuant to paragraph 2, point (a), and to developing methods of calculating embedded emissions based on environmental footprint methods.
uncertainties.reasoning: Generic, undefined stakeholder consultation for policy-development and reporting purposes; no institutionally defined intermediary function.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: The Commission shall establish a CBAM registry of authorised CBAM declarants in the form of a standardised electronic database containing the data regarding the CBAM certificates of those authorised CBAM declarants.
uncertainties.reasoning: The registry and the common central platform are electronic systems/instruments the Commission operates, not actors.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: the Commission shall evaluate and report on how the financing under that Regulation has contributed to the decarbonisation of the manufacturing industry in LDCs.
uncertainties.reasoning: The substantive technical-assistance mechanism for developing countries and LDCs is established under a different, external instrument (Regulation (EU) 2021/947, NDICI-Global Europe) not reproduced in this corpus; this Act only requires Commission reporting on that instrument's effects.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: mutual recognition and peer evaluation of the accreditation bodies
uncertainties.reasoning: A horizontal peer-review mechanism among accreditation bodies themselves; reinforces rather than separately establishes REL_C02_002's intermediation finding.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: An operator may disclose the information on the verification of embedded emissions referred to in paragraph 5 of this Article to an authorised CBAM declarant. The authorised CBAM declarant shall be entitled to use that disclosed information in order to fulfil the obligation referred to in Article 8.
candidate_actors: operators of installations in third countries
uncertainties.reasoning: Voluntary information-sharing between two independently regulated targets (operator and declarant), not a third-party intermediary structure feeding R's regulation of T.
